key_rules_and_shortcuts: Compass span locks an exact radius distance for transfer.
All points on a circle boundary are equidistant (radius r) from the center point.
Set-squares (45°-45°-90° and 30°-60°-90°) are used for drawing exact 90° perpendiculars.
unit_conversions_and_definitions: Radius: Span distance between pivot needle and pencil tip

section_2_common_pitfalls_and_error_anal.frequent_exam_mistake: Allowing the compass pivot needle to shift while tracing a circle.
section_2_common_pitfalls_and_error_anal.why_it_happens: Applying too much pressure on the pencil arm instead of holding the top pivot handle.
section_2_common_pitfalls_and_error_anal.correct_exam_approach: Hold the compass exclusively by its top hinge handle and rotate smoothly.

level_1_objective_and_recall_1_mark.question: What is the diameter of a circle whose compass radius was set to 4.5 cm?

level_2_direct_computational_2_marks.question: Write the step-by-step construction for drawing two concentric circles of radii 3 cm and 5 cm.
step_by_step_solution: Set compass to 3 cm, fix needle at O, draw inner circle.
Set compass to 5 cm, fix needle at same center O, draw outer circle.

level_3_multi_step_word_problems_3_to_5_.problem_statement: Construct a rectangle ABCD with AB = 6 cm and BC = 4 cm using ruler and set-square.
solution_working: Step 1: Draw segment AB = 6 cm using ruler.
Step 2: Place set-square along AB at A and draw perpendicular ray.
Step 3: Measure 4 cm along ray to locate point D.
Step 4: Repeat perpendicular at B to mark C at 4 cm.

level_4_hots_and_competency_case_studies.case_scenario_text: Case Study: Inscribing Regular Hexagon. A student draws a circle of radius 4 cm.

sub_questions.question: How can the student construct a regular hexagon inside this circle using only compass step transfers?
sub_questions.detailed_solution: Keep compass opening at radius 4 cm. Starting at any point on circumference, mark consecutive 4 cm arcs around the circle. The 6 arc intersections divide the circle into 6 equal parts forming a regular hexagon.
